- Measure first: run `pytest --durations=10` or `jest --runTestsByPath tests/slow.test.js` to identify the slowest files.
- Parallelize tests: run `pytest -n auto`, `jest --maxWorkers=50%`, `go test -parallel 8`, or `mvn -T 1C test`.
- Split slow tests: mark them with `@pytest.mark.slow` and run `pytest -m "not slow"` locally.
- Use faster test runners: run `pytest -q --tb=no --no-header` locally and reserve verbose output for CI.
- Cache dependencies: run `pip install -r requirements.txt --cache-dir .cache/pip` or `npm ci --cache .npm-cache`.
- Replace real databases: set `DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///:memory:` or use `pytest-postgresql` with `--postgresql-template1`.
- Mock network calls: patch `requests.get` with `unittest.mock.patch("requests.get")` or use `responses.add(responses.GET, "https://api.example.com", json={})`.
- Mock external services: use `fakeredis.FakeStrictRedis()` instead of Redis, `mongomock.MongoClient()` instead of MongoDB, or `moto.mock_s3()` instead of AWS S3.
- Reduce fixture cost: use `@pytest.fixture(scope="session")` for immutable data and `scope="module"` for shared read-only state.
- Avoid repeated setup: create one `pytest.fixture(scope="session")` for app config instead of rebuilding it in every test.
- Use factories: generate test data with `factory_boy` instead of copying large JSON fixtures.
- Delete redundant tests: run `grep -R "def test_" tests/ | wc -l` and remove duplicate assertions.
- Merge tiny tests: combine related assertions into one test function such as `test_user_signup_and_login()`.
- Use `--lf`: run `pytest --lf` to rerun only failed tests during debugging.
- Use `--sw`: run `pytest --sw` to execute slowest tests first and fail fast.
- Use `--collect-only`: run `pytest --collect-only -q` to find import-time slowdowns.
- Use `--import-mode=importlib`: run `pytest --import-mode=importlib` to reduce path-scanning overhead.
- Disable coverage locally: run `pytest --no-cov` and enable `pytest --cov=app --cov-report=xml` only in CI.
- Use ephemeral temp dirs: set `pytest --basetemp=/tmp/pytest` to avoid slow cleanup paths.
- Use in-memory storage: set `CACHE_BACKEND=memory` or `SESSION_ENGINE=django.contrib.sessions.backends.cache`.
- Use smaller test data: replace `tests/fixtures/large_dataset.json` with `tests/fixtures/small

Share your release docs or use this default release process.

- Confirm inputs: `CHANGELOG.md`, `package.json`, `git log --oneline v1.2.0..HEAD`.
- Create branch: `git switch -c release/2026-06-15 main`.
- Bump version: `npm version patch --no-git-tag-version`.
- Update changelog: `git-chglog -o CHANGELOG.md`.
- Run CI: `gh workflow run release.yml -f version=1.3.0`.
- Smoke test staging: `curl -fsS https://staging.example.com/healthz`.
- Deploy production: `kubectl rollout status deployment/app -n prod`.
- Tag release: `git tag v1.3.0 && git push origin v1.3.0`.
- Publish notes: `gh release create v1.3.0 --generate-notes`.
- Roll back if needed: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/app -n prod`.

Send `release.yml`, `Makefile`, `package.json`, or `docs/release.md` for your exact process.

## Evidence
- Load testing showed p99 latency fell from 842 ms to 521 ms when queue depth was capped at 256 and producer throughput was limited to 1,200 msg/s.
## Next
- Deploy a 256-item bounded queue with a 1,200 msg/s producer limit to staging and monitor p99 latency for 24 hours.
